cleanIntro: The Mark V is Weatherby's own action — nine locking lugs, a very short bolt lift, and a bolt that comes apart quite differently from anything else in the catalogue. Two Mark V specifics govern this job. THE BOLT IS RELEASED BY PULLING THE TRIGGER, not by a bolt release lever; that is the Vanguard's method, the two Weatherby books are laid out almost identically, and confusing them is the easiest mistake to make here. And the bolt teardown runs on a firing pin RETAINING BALL — a loose ball bearing that will disappear into the carpet if the bolt is stripped over a bare bench. Weatherby's instruction is that the rifle must be disassembled before it can be properly cleaned, and that further disassembly beyond what follows is not recommended.

steps.title: Safety OFF SAFE, bolt up and back — the round comes out
steps.action: Muzzle safe, fingers clear of the trigger guard. Move the manual safety lever to OFF SAFE, lift the bolt handle until it stops and draw the bolt rearward against the bolt stop. The Mark V's bolt lift is unusually short, so the handle reaching its stop happens sooner than you expect — go by the stop, not by the angle.
steps.quote: 2. To remove a cartridge from the chamber, open the bolt by lifting the bolt handle until it stops and pulling the bolt to the rear until the bolt stops against the bolt stop. The cartridge will be ejected from the receiver.
steps.cite: MARK V® — Owner's Manual — Nov 2021 (date carried in the published filename and in the Weatherby index label "Mark V (USA-TriggerTech 11.2021-present)") — Unloading the Rifle — p.10

steps.title: Prove the chamber gave the case up
steps.action: Check the chamber by eye and by finger. If a live round or a fired case is still in there once the bolt has come back, Weatherby's instruction is to remove the bolt and take the rifle to a service centre or gunsmith, keeping the bolt out of the rifle. Do not attempt to force it out.
steps.quote: 3. Visually and manually check to make certain that the bolt has extracted any live round or fired cartridge case from the chamber. If a live round or fired cartridge case remains in the chamber, remove the bolt, (refer to Removing The Bolt Assembly From The Receiver, page 8) and immediately take the rifle to a Weatherby service center or a qualified gunsmith, keeping the bolt out of the rifle at all times.
steps.cite: MARK V® — Owner's Manual — Nov 2021 (date carried in the published filename and in the Weatherby index label "Mark V (USA-TriggerTech 11.2021-present)") — Unloading the Rifle — p.10

steps.title: Floorplate release, magazine emptied into your hand
steps.action: Depress the floorplate release lever and the floorplate swings open, dropping the magazine column out. Catch the cartridges rather than letting them fall — Weatherby's own reasoning is that a damaged or dirtied round can end up jammed live in the chamber, which is a far worse problem than a scuffed bullet.
steps.quote: 4. To unload the magazine, open the floorplate by depressing the floorplate release lever (refer to Fig. 4). The floorplate will swing out, allowing the cartridges to drop free. Do not allow the cartridges to fall to the ground as they may be damaged or become dirty, making loading and chambering more difficult. Subsequent loading of a damaged or dirty cartridge may cause a live round to become jammed in the chamber of the firearm, resulting in an unsafe condition.
steps.cite: MARK V® — Owner's Manual — Nov 2021 (date carried in the published filename and in the Weatherby index label "Mark V (USA-TriggerTech 11.2021-present)") — Unloading the Rifle — p.10

steps.title: Reconfirm, reseat the follower, close the floorplate
steps.action: Look and feel through the magazine box and the chamber once more, push the follower back down into the box, and close the floorplate until it latches. Weatherby's warning on this page is blunt about why: a bolt pushed fully forward over a loaded magazine chambers a round and the rifle can then be fired.
steps.quote: 5. Visually and manually reconfirm that there are no cartridges remaining in the magazine or chamber. 6. Reposition the magazine follower inside the magazine box and close the floorplate.
steps.cite: MARK V® — Owner's Manual — Nov 2021 (date carried in the published filename and in the Weatherby index label "Mark V (USA-TriggerTech 11.2021-present)") — Unloading the Rifle — p.10

steps.title: Bolt fully back, and LOOK before a screw turns
steps.action: Unload the rifle, set the safety lever to OFF SAFE, raise the bolt handle and draw the bolt all the way to the rear. Then visually check the chamber and the magazine to be certain there are no cartridges in the rifle. Weatherby sets this instruction in capitals at the head of the Mark V disassembly, which is where it belongs.
steps.quote: 1. Unload the rifle (refer to Unloading the Rifle, page 10). 2. Move the safety lever to the “OFF SAFE” position (refer to Manual Safety Operation, page 6). 3. Raise the bolt handle and draw the bolt all the way to the rear. 4. VISUALLY CHECK THE CHAMBER AND THE MAGAZINE TO BE CERTAIN THERE ARE NO CARTRIDGES IN THE RIFLE.
steps.cite: MARK V® — Owner's Manual — Nov 2021 (date carried in the published filename and in the Weatherby index label "Mark V (USA-TriggerTech 11.2021-present)") — Disassembly of the Mark V Rifle — p.11

steps.title: PULL THE TRIGGER to release the bolt, then draw it out
steps.action: With the rifle proven empty, the safety OFF SAFE and the bolt held against the bolt stop, pull the trigger fully rearward and hold it while you draw the bolt straight back out of the receiver. On a Mark V the trigger IS the bolt release — there is no release lever to press. This is the one step where you deliberately pull the trigger, and it is why every check above had to come first.
steps.prose: The Vanguard in Weatherby's other book uses a bolt release lever instead. Same maker, same page layout, different mechanism — do not carry one method onto the other rifle.
steps.quote: 5. Pull the trigger rearward as far as possible 6. Move the bolt straight rearward until the bolt clears the receiver
steps.cite: MARK V® — Owner's Manual — Nov 2021 (date carried in the published filename and in the Weatherby index label "Mark V (USA-TriggerTech 11.2021-present)") — Removing the Bolt Assembly from Receiver — p.8

steps.title: Floorplate open, both trigger guard screws out, stock off
steps.action: Press the floorplate latch to open the floorplate — the front trigger guard screw sits behind it. Take out the front and rear trigger guard screws with a properly fitting screwdriver, lift the trigger guard assembly out of the stock, and separate the stock from the barrelled action. Keep the screws identified; they are not the same length.
steps.quote:
a. Press the floorplate latch (refer to Fig. 4) to open the floorplate. b. With a screwdriver of the proper size, remove the front and rear trigger
guard screws. c. Remove the trigger guard assembly from the stock. d. Remove the stock.
steps.cite: MARK V® — Owner's Manual — Nov 2021 (date carried in the published filename and in the Weatherby index label "Mark V (USA-TriggerTech 11.2021-present)") — Disassembly of the Mark V Rifle — p.11

steps.title: Cocking piece back onto its engaging shoulder
steps.action: Take a square-faced object and push the cocking piece rearward out of its fired position, then rotate it onto its engaging shoulder in the bolt sleeve. That rotation is what parks the mainspring under control before anything unscrews. Get this wrong and the firing pin assembly is still live when you start on the bolt sleeve lock.
steps.quote: 2. Using a square-faced object, push the cocking piece from its post-firing position (refer to Fig. 5) to the rear, and rotate it onto its engaging shoulder in the bolt sleeve (refer to Fig. 6).
steps.cite: MARK V® — Owner's Manual — Nov 2021 (date carried in the published filename and in the Weatherby index label "Mark V (USA-TriggerTech 11.2021-present)") — Disassembly of the Bolt Assembly — p.11

steps.title: Bolt sleeve lock in, unscrew until the retaining ball shows
steps.action: Push the bolt sleeve lock in with a blunt object or a fingertip to disengage it, then unscrew the bolt body a few turns from the bolt sleeve — only far enough that the firing pin RETAINING BALL is completely exposed. Stop there and look; the ball is small, loose and the one part in this rifle you cannot improvise a replacement for.
steps.caution: Failure to strictly adhere to the disassembly and assembly instructions contained herein
steps.quote: 3. Disengage the bolt sleeve lock (refer to Fig. 7) by pushing it in with a blunt object or finger and unscrew the bolt a few turns until the firing pin retaining ball is completely exposed (refer to Fig. 7).
steps.cite: MARK V® — Owner's Manual — Nov 2021 (date carried in the published filename and in the Weatherby index label "Mark V (USA-TriggerTech 11.2021-present)") — Disassembly of the Bolt Assembly — p.11

steps.title: Retaining ball out, bolt body off — field strip complete
steps.action: Lift the retaining ball out with the bolt sleeve hole facing UP and put it somewhere it cannot roll, then unscrew the bolt body completely from the bolt sleeve. That is the Mark V's published strip: barrelled action, stock, trigger guard assembly, bolt body, bolt sleeve with firing pin and cocking piece, and the retaining ball. Weatherby stops here — further disassembly is not recommended and could damage the rifle; anything more goes to a Weatherby Authorized Service Center or a qualified gunsmith.
steps.aside: 4. Remove the retaining ball and unscrew the bolt body completely from the bolt sleeve.
steps.quote: Further disassembly is not recommended and could result in damage to your rifle. If further disassembly is required, please contact a Weatherby Authorized Service Center or qualified gunsmith.
steps.cite: MARK V® — Owner's Manual — Nov 2021 (date carried in the published filename and in the Weatherby index label "Mark V (USA-TriggerTech 11.2021-present)") — Disassembly of the Bolt Assembly — p.11

steps.title: Bore from the chamber end, brush centred at the muzzle
steps.action: With the bolt out, run a properly sized solvent-wet bore brush from the CHAMBER end all the way out of the muzzle and carefully back, keeping the brush centred as it leaves the muzzle so the crown is not damaged. Repeat several times, then switch to patches on a jag, again from the chamber end, until they come out clean.
steps.quote: 3. Starting from the chamber end, push the cleaning rod all the way through the bore, allowing it to exit the muzzle, then carefully draw it back through the bore, ensuring that the brush stays centered in the muzzle as it is withdrawn. Repeat several times.
steps.cite: MARK V® — Owner's Manual — Nov 2021 (date carried in the published filename and in the Weatherby index label "Mark V (USA-TriggerTech 11.2021-present)") — Cleaning the Bore — p.13

steps.title: Lubricant patch, then a dry patch to take it back out
steps.action: One lubricant-saturated patch through from the chamber end, then a dry clean patch behind it. The dry patch is the point of the exercise: standing oil in a bore or chamber can raise pressures or act as a partial obstruction. Finish by wiping a light film of lubricant around the muzzle itself.
steps.quote: 7. Insert a patch saturated with gun lubricant into the cleaning rod tip and push it through the bore from the chamber end. Remove the patch and withdraw the rod. 8. Insert a dry, clean patch into the cleaning rod tip and push it through the bore starting at the chamber end to remove excess lubricant. Remove the patch and withdraw the rod.
steps.cite: MARK V® — Owner's Manual — Nov 2021 (date carried in the published filename and in the Weatherby index label "Mark V (USA-TriggerTech 11.2021-present)") — Cleaning the Bore — p.13
steps.warn: Excess lubrication in the bore or chamber of any firearm may create excessive chamber pressures or a partial bore obstruction, resulting in possible damage to the firearm and serious injury to the shooter and bystanders upon firing. BE SURE ALL EXCESS LUBRICANT HAS BEEN REMOVED.

steps.title: Receiver recesses and the bolt parts
steps.action: Clean the inside and outside of the receiver with solvent on a small lint-free cloth and a plastic-bristle brush into the recesses — the Mark V's nine-lug raceways hold more residue than a two-lug action does, so work them. Dry, then a light coat of lubricant with the excess taken off. Clean the bolt parts the same way, with a small brush into the bolt sleeve recesses and around the firing pin spring.
steps.aside: 1. Using a small lint-free cloth, clean the inside and outside of the receiver with gun-cleaning solvent and dry thoroughly with a clean cloth. Use of a plastic bristle gun cleaning brush will help to clean the recesses of the receiver.
steps.quote: 1. Clean all parts with a gun cleaning solvent and dry with a clean cloth. Use of a small brush will help in cleaning the recesses of the bolt sleeve and the firing pin spring.
steps.cite: MARK V® — Owner's Manual — Nov 2021 (date carried in the published filename and in the Weatherby index label "Mark V (USA-TriggerTech 11.2021-present)") — Cleaning of the Bolt Assembly — p.12

steps.title: Trigger assembly: compressed air ONLY, no oil
steps.action: Blow the trigger's internals clear with compressed air and put nothing else near it. Weatherby states that no lubrication is required inside the trigger assembly; if oil has got in, the fix is more air and a wipe. Eye protection on while the air line is running.
steps.quote: Using compressed air, blow the internal components of the trigger assembly off to remove any loose dirt and debris. No lubrication is required on the internal components of the trigger assembly. If oil seeps into the trigger housing, blow out the internals with compressed air again and wipe off any excess oil residue.
steps.cite: MARK V® — Owner's Manual — Nov 2021 (date carried in the published filename and in the Weatherby index label "Mark V (USA-TriggerTech 11.2021-present)") — Cleaning the Trigger Assembly — p.15
steps.warn: Always wear eye protection when using compressed air to avoid injury to eyes by foreign objects.

steps.title: Magazine, trigger guard, stock and rust
steps.action: Solvent and a lint-free cloth through the magazine box, follower and spring, dried, then lightly lubricated. Brush the trigger guard assembly's exposed surfaces with solvent and dry. The stock normally wants nothing more than a dry or silicone cloth — but no acetone or abrasive cleaners on a carbon fibre stock, and after a wet outing let everything dry for two to three hours before oiling.
steps.caution: DO NOT ALLOW RUST TO GO UNTREATED!
steps.quote: NOTE: Do not use acetone or any abrasive solvent cleaners on carbon fiber stocks. This can jeopardize the external coating of the carbon fiber.
steps.cite: MARK V® — Owner's Manual — Nov 2021 (date carried in the published filename and in the Weatherby index label "Mark V (USA-TriggerTech 11.2021-present)") — Cleaning the Stock — p.15

deepAbsentReason: The Mark V book's own limit is reached at the end of the bolt disassembly: further disassembly is not recommended and could result in damage to the rifle, with anything beyond it referred to a Weatherby Authorized Service Center or a qualified gunsmith. Everything Weatherby publishes for this rifle — including the bolt teardown to the firing pin retaining ball, which is deeper than most makers publish at all — is already in the walked steps above. There is no further published procedure to branch to.

cleaning.name: Bore
tasks: Bolt out first; clean from the CHAMBER end only.
Solvent-wet brush through and back, kept centred in the muzzle on the way out to protect the crown.
Patches on a jag, chamber end, until clean.
All solvent off the muzzle; one lubricant patch, then a dry patch to remove the excess.
Light film of lubricant around the muzzle.

cleaning.name: Barrel exterior and receiver
tasks: Solvent-wet cloth over all accessible barrel and receiver surfaces; brush the corners and the nine-lug raceways.
All solvent removed with a dry lint-free cloth.
Light lubricant coat, excess wiped off.
Screw-off muzzle brake if fitted: unscrew counter-clockwise viewed from the muzzle; brush the brake's bore, threads and exterior.

cleaning.name: Bolt assembly
tasks: All parts in solvent, then dried.
Small brush into the bolt sleeve recesses and around the firing pin spring.
Light gun oil on all accessible surfaces, excess removed.
Account for the firing pin retaining ball before you move the parts — it is loose and it rolls.

cleaning.name: Magazine and trigger guard
tasks: Magazine box interior, follower and spring cleaned with solvent and dried.
Light lubricant inside the magazine and on the follower and spring, excess removed.
Trigger guard assembly brushed with solvent and dried.

cleaning.name: Trigger assembly
tasks: Compressed air only.
No lubrication inside the trigger assembly.
Oil that has seeped in: blow out again and wipe the residue.
Eye protection while using compressed air.

cleaning.name: Stock and rust prevention
tasks: Dry cloth or silicone cloth normally suffices.
No acetone or abrasive solvent cleaners on carbon fibre stocks.
After exposure to rain or snow: 2-3 hours at room temperature to dry, then a liberal coat of high-grade gun oil, excess wiped off.
Surface rust: plastic-bristle brush and solvent; if it will not lift, a service centre or gunsmith. Do not leave rust untreated.

reassembly: Bolt sleeve held horizontal with the retaining ball hole UP.

Cocking piece held firmly on its engaging shoulder; rotate the firing pin clockwise until one of the firing pin grooves sits directly under the retaining ball hole and the firing pin end is flush with the rear surface of the cocking piece.
Check that flush condition before going further — Weatherby asks for it as a separate step.
Retaining ball into the retaining ball hole in the bolt sleeve.
Bolt body screwed onto the bolt sleeve until the bolt sleeve lock stops it.
Bolt sleeve lock pushed in with a blunt object or finger, then keep screwing until the bolt sleeve stops against the bolt body.
Unscrew the bolt body counter-clockwise until the bolt sleeve lock aligns with the bolt sleeve detent slot in the end of the bolt body.
Rotate the cocking piece off the engaging shoulder so the firing pin assembly can move forward.
Barrelled action into the stock; trigger guard assembly and both screws refitted per the book's Assembly of Weatherby Mark V Rifle section.
fncheck: With the rifle proven empty and the muzzle safe: cycle the bolt several times and confirm the short Mark V lift, the full rearward travel to the bolt stop and a clean lock-up on closing. Confirm the bolt sleeve lock has engaged its detent slot — a bolt reassembled without it can unscrew in use. Work the safety lever through its positions and confirm each is positive. Open and close the floorplate and confirm it latches. Check the bore is clear of patches and standing oil before the rifle is loaded.
